title: Cross-model KV warmup litmus for tokens/sec microbench suite
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Create and maintain a tokens-per-second microbenchmark (litmus) that specifically measures cross-model throughput impact from KV-cache warmup and prefix saturation patterns. The goal is a standardized harness that can: (1) produce reproducible TPS and p95 numbers for core models across hardware variants, (2) detect regressions in p95 or sustained tokens/sec via CI gates, and (3) provide telemetry and artifacts for root-cause analysis (trace IDs, kernel selection, batch distributions). This ticket covers design, implementation, CI integration, and initial onboarding of 3 core model families.
acceptance_criteria: Bench harness can run deterministically in CI and produce tokens/sec and p95 for a configured model+profile within 10 minutes
Regression detector raises a failing CI check if p95 increases by >10% or median tokens/sec drops by >12% versus the runway baseline
KV-warmup experiments (cold -> warmed) are reproducible: cold and warm runs' delta documented and within expected bounds per model
Artifacts stored per run: stdout logs, kernel selection summary, batch size distribution, kv-cache hit/miss stats, and a compact token-rate timeseries
Dashboard tiles added to Console staging showing historical p95 and tokens/sec with alert rules wired to oncall Slack channel
Runbook describing when to ignore transient regressions (e.g., infra noise) and steps to bisect commits is checked in
At least 3 core models onboarded with profiles and baselines committed to artifacts storage
tasks: Design workload matrix: models, sequence lengths, prompt shapes (single short, long prefix, multi-turn), KV warmup stages
Implement harness runner that supports jittered concurrency, steady-state pacing, and KV-cache reset/warm paths
Add structured log outputs and artifact packaging (json lines for metrics + zipped traces)
Integrate regression-detector job into core CI (fail-on-threshold with opt-out tag)
Create baseline artifact store path and versioning schema
Wire Console dashboard and paging alerts for p95 spikes and sustained throughput drops
Onboard first three core model configs and capture baseline runs

notes: This harness is intentionally conservative: CI will run in 'dry-fail' mode for the first month (annotate regressions rather than block) while we calibrate thresholds. Post-calibration, we will flip to blocking for high-severity model families. Future work: expose per-model quantization-aware profiles and add end-to-end production canary runs tied to Dedicated capacity pools.
